questions.prompt: According to the QRC, recovery from a FULL stall is started at which indication?
choices: Nose and/or wing drop, or an (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the green arc, whichever comes first
The first buffet, followed by a second buffet to confirm
questions.explanation: The QRC 'Recovery of the stall is started at' table states that for a full stall recovery begins at nose and/or wing drop or (excessive) rate of descent with full back pressure. The other criteria belong to the approach to stall (landing and clean configurations).

questions.prompt: State the minimum altitudes by which a FULL stall must be recovered (dual and solo).
questions.explanation: The pre-stall checklist Altitude item states: Full Stall recovered before Dual 2000 ft AGL, Solo 3000 ft AGL.

questions.prompt: State the minimum altitudes by which an APPROACH to the stall must be recovered (dual and solo).
questions.explanation: The pre-stall checklist Altitude item states: Approach to the Stall recovered before Dual 1500 ft AGL, Solo 2500 ft AGL.

questions.prompt: Recite the complete pre-stall checklist: all four inside inspection items (with their required states) and all four outside inspection items.
questions.model_answer: Inside inspection: 1. Trim - Checked (trimmed for level flight); 2. Flaps - Retracted (UP); 3. Engine - Checked (instruments in green, fuel balanced); 4. Security - Checked (harnesses tight, baggage stowed). Outside inspection: 1. Altitude - Checked; 2. Position - Checked; 3. Orientation - Checked; 4. Sky - Free.
questions.explanation: The QRC pre-stall checklist lists these four inside items (Trim, Flaps, Engine, Security) and four outside items (Altitude, Position, Orientation, Sky), to be performed before every stall and every approach to the stall.

questions.prompt: The Position item of the pre-stall checklist says you must never stall above which of the following?
choices: 3/8 cloud or less
Open, unpopulated farmland
4/8 clouds or more
Any area outside controlled airspace
questions.explanation: The QRC Position item lists: never stall above built up areas, harbours and industrial areas, populated areas, airports/CTRs, extended water areas, 4/8 clouds or more, and other traffic. '4/8 clouds or more' is the only option on that list.

questions.prompt: For the Sky item of the pre-stall checklist, which clearing turns does the QRC prescribe to check the airspace ahead and below for other traffic?
choices: Two 180-degree turns, one in each direction
45-degree right and left clearing turns
A single 360-degree turn to the left
90-degree right and left clearing turns, or a left-hand 180-degree turn
questions.explanation: The QRC Sky item states: make 90-degree right and left clearing turns or a left-hand 180-degree turn to check the airspace ahead and below for other traffic.

questions.prompt: Put the full stall recovery WITH power (clean) in the correct order.
steps: Pitch down to reduce the angle of attack, simultaneously call "RECOVER"
Check for increasing speed (about 70 KIAS)
Pitch up gently while moving the power lever gently forward to reach full power when the nose is passing through the horizon
Maintain coordinated flight using rudder (ball centered)
Pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS)
Climb back to original altitude
questions.explanation: This is the QRC 'Full stall recovery with power (clean)' sequence: reduce AoA and call RECOVER, confirm speed increasing (about 70 KIAS), full power as the nose passes the horizon, stay coordinated, pitch for 80 KIAS climb and regain the original altitude.

questions.prompt: Recovery from the approach to stall in the LANDING configuration is started at:
choices: Full back pressure with an excessive rate of descent
The nose or wing dropping through the horizon
5 KIAS below the bottom of the white arc
Stall warning, buffet, or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: The QRC states for approach to stall in the landing configuration: recover at the stall warning, buffet or 5 KIAS above the bottom of the white arc, whichever comes first. Nose/wing drop with full back pressure is the full-stall criterion.

questions.prompt: In the approach to stall in the landing configuration, below which speeds are the flap selections made (after calling "SPEED CHECKED")?
questions.explanation: The QRC approach-to-stall (landing configuration) procedure: check speed below 108 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" and select flaps take-off; check speed below 91 KIAS, call "SPEED CHECKED" and select flaps landing.

questions.prompt: During the recovery from an approach to stall in the landing configuration, when are the flaps retracted fully up?
choices: Immediately with the application of full power
When the speed is above 70 KIAS, after selecting flaps take-off
When the speed is above 91 KIAS
Only after reaching the original altitude
questions.explanation: The QRC recovery sequence: full power, pitch for climb attitude, select flaps take-off, then at speed >70 KIAS select flaps up, then climb back to the previous altitude.

questions.prompt: Which bank angles does the QRC prescribe for the approach-to-stall manoeuvres in turns?
choices: Descending turn in approach configuration: 20 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 15 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 30 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 20 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 15 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 20 degrees
Descending turn in approach configuration: 45 degrees; climbing turn with flaps retracted: 30 degrees
questions.explanation: The QRC states: start the descending turn in approach configuration with 20 degrees of bank, and start the climbing turn with flaps retracted with 15 degrees of bank. 30 degrees is the normal/descending cruise-turn bank and 45 degrees is the steep-turn bank used elsewhere in the QRC.

questions.prompt: In the full stall recovery WITHOUT power (clean), after the pitch-down and "RECOVER" call with speed increasing through about 70 KIAS, you adjust pitch for:
choices: Climb attitude at 80 KIAS
Glide attitude at 75 KIAS, and trim
Cruise descent at 110 KIAS
Approach descent at 90 KIAS
questions.explanation: The QRC full stall recovery without power: pitch down, call "RECOVER", check increasing speed (about 70 KIAS), maintain coordination, then adjust pitch for glide attitude (75 KIAS) and trim; when established in the glide, end the exercise and climb back to the original altitude.

questions.prompt: What are the FIRST actions of the wing dip recovery in the QRC?
choices: Apply full opposite rudder, then pitch down
Apply full power and roll wings level with ailerons
Power idle, ailerons neutral
Pull up gently while applying full power
questions.explanation: Wing dip recovery step 1 in the QRC is: power idle, ailerons neutral. Full opposite rudder comes only after the "Recover" call with pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall.

questions.prompt: Put the wing dip recovery in the correct order.
steps: Power idle, ailerons neutral
Call "Recover" and simultaneously pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall
Apply full opposite rudder with the feet
Neutralize the rudder with the feet when rotation stops
Check for increasing speed (about 80 KIAS)
Pull gently out of the dive, moving the power lever gently forward to reach full power when the nose passes through the horizon
Direction with the feet, no bank; adjust pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS) and climb back to the previous altitude
questions.explanation: This follows the QRC wing dip recovery: idle power and neutral ailerons first, break the stall with pitch down below glide attitude while calling "Recover", stop rotation with full opposite rudder, neutralize rudder when rotation stops, confirm about 80 KIAS, then recover from the dive reaching full power at the horizon and climb at 80 KIAS.

questions.prompt: During the wing dip recovery, at about what speed do you check for increasing speed before pulling out of the dive?
choices: About 70 KIAS
About 75 KIAS
About 90 KIAS
About 80 KIAS
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery step 5 is: check for increasing speed (about 80 KIAS). 70 KIAS is the speed check in the full stall recovery; 75 KIAS is the glide speed.

questions.prompt: Put the QRC emergency (spin) recovery procedure - 'just in case you don't know the procedure anymore' - in the correct order.
steps: Power idle
Ailerons and elevator neutral
Apply full opposite rudder against the rotation
Neutralize the rudder
Pull gently out of the dive, wings level
Full power when the nose is passing the horizon
Climb back to the desired altitude
questions.explanation: This is the verbatim QRC emergency recovery sequence: power idle, ailerons and elevator neutral, full opposite rudder against rotation, neutralize rudder, pull gently out of the dive with wings level, full power at the horizon, climb back to the desired altitude.

questions.prompt: The QRC general emergency recovery procedure is stated to be applicable for:
choices: All aircraft, regardless of certification or loading
All JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided mass & balance falls in the envelope and the aircraft is trimmed for cruise flight
Only the Diamond DA40-TDI, in any loading condition
All JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided the aircraft is trimmed for approach
questions.explanation: The QRC states the general procedure is applicable for all JAR23 & FAR23 approved aircraft, provided mass & balance falls in the envelope and the aircraft is trimmed for cruise flight, and directs the pilot to consult the AFM/Diamond for the DA40 specific procedure.

questions.prompt: In the wing dip recovery, when do you neutralize the rudder?
choices: When the rotation stops
As soon as full opposite rudder is applied
When the speed reaches 80 KIAS
When the nose passes through the horizon
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery: apply full opposite rudder with the feet, then neutralize the rudder with the feet when rotation stops.

questions.prompt: With the "Recover" call in the wing dip recovery, you simultaneously pitch down:
choices: To the horizon, then hold level
Below the climb attitude
Below the glide attitude, to break the stall
To the normal cruise attitude
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery step 2: call "Recover" and simultaneously pitch down below the glide attitude to break the stall.

questions.prompt: After the rotation has stopped in the wing dip recovery, how is direction controlled while pulling out of the dive?
choices: With ailerons, rolling into a 20-degree bank
With the feet (rudder), no bank
With ailerons only, keeping the ball centered
With differential braking
questions.explanation: The QRC wing dip recovery states: direction with feet, no bank, then adjust pitch for climb attitude (80 KIAS) and climb back to the previous altitude.

questions.prompt: What is the correct first call and first action for a rejected take-off?
choices: Call "Going-around!" and apply full power
Make the RT call first, then close the power
Call "RECOVER" and apply full brakes
Call "Aborting!" and close the power immediately
questions.explanation: The QRC rejected take-off: step 1 call out "Aborting!", step 2 close the power immediately, then maintain the centreline with rudder, brake as necessary, elevator neutral/aileron into the wind, RT call, and vacate the runway as soon as practical.

questions.prompt: Put the rejected take-off procedure in the correct order.
steps: Call out: "Aborting!"
Close the power immediately
Maintain runway centreline using the rudder
Apply brakes as necessary
Elevator neutral / aileron into the wind
RT call: "call sign, rejected take-off"
Vacate the runway as soon as practical
questions.explanation: This is the verbatim QRC rejected take-off sequence, from the "Aborting!" call and immediate power closure through braking, the rejected take-off RT call, and vacating the runway.

questions.prompt: Put the simulated engine failure after take-off (SEFATO) procedure in the correct order.
steps: Pitch for the glide attitude
Select a landing area and avoid obstacles
Troubleshoot (time permitting)
Select flaps take-off when the landing is assured
Adjust attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps)
Plan a full flaps landing
Crash drill
Touchdown
questions.explanation: This is the QRC SEFATO sequence: glide attitude, landing area selection, troubleshooting time permitting, flaps T/O when landing is assured, 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps), full flaps landing planned, crash drill, touchdown. For an actual failure: evacuate and call RAC; for training: go-around at minimum safe height.

questions.prompt: In the SEFATO procedure, which approach speeds does the QRC prescribe?
choices: 75 KIAS, or 70 KIAS with flaps
80 KIAS, or 70 KIAS with flaps
75 KIAS, or 60 KIAS with flaps
90 KIAS, or 75 KIAS with flaps
questions.explanation: The QRC SEFATO step: adjust attitude for 75 KIAS (70 KIAS with flaps).

questions.prompt: For the glide-in from circuit altitude, how does the QRC modify the downwind leg?
choices: Flaps take-off selected, speed 90 KIAS
No flaps on downwind, speed 75 KIAS
Flaps landing selected, speed 75 KIAS
No flaps on downwind, speed 90 KIAS
questions.explanation: The QRC glide-in procedure: fly the standard circuit but with no flaps on downwind at 90 KIAS, maintain circuit altitude on downwind/base depending on wind, close the power lever when the landing is assured, then glide at 75 KIAS.

questions.prompt: In the glide-in from circuit altitude, the QRC has you plan a full flaps landing with touchdown at:
choices: 70 KIAS
75 KIAS
60 KIAS
65 KIAS
questions.explanation: The QRC glide-in procedure: glide speed 75 KIAS, select flaps when the landing is assured, plan a full flaps landing and touch down at 60 KIAS. 65 KIAS is the short field landing approach speed and 70 KIAS the normal final speed.

questions.prompt: State the QRC flapless landing speeds on each circuit leg.
questions.explanation: The QRC flapless landing: maintain 90 KIAS on downwind, 85 KIAS on base leg, power/attitude 75 KIAS on final, with a nose attitude higher than for a normal landing and no flare-out at touchdown.

questions.prompt: Which technique does the QRC prescribe for the touchdown phase of a flapless landing?
choices: Do not flare out; maintain a slightly higher nose attitude during touchdown
Normal flare to a full-stall touchdown on the main wheels
Hold the aircraft off as long as possible at 60 KIAS
Close the power only after touchdown, in the tempo of the flare
questions.explanation: The QRC flapless landing states: nose attitude higher than for a normal landing, and do not flare out - maintain a slightly higher attitude during touchdown. Closing power in the tempo of the flare belongs to the short field landing.

questions.prompt: How does the QRC define a wave-off, and what does it say about the wheels?
choices: A go-around below 100 ft AGL; the wheels must never touch the runway
A go-around below 50 ft AGL; due to aircraft inertia the main wheels may briefly touch the runway - do not pull back excessively to prevent this, and do not deliberately land
A go-around below 50 ft AGL; if the wheels touch, you are committed to land
A rejected landing at any height; a brief touchdown always ends the manoeuvre
questions.explanation: The QRC wave-off: it is a go-around below 50 ft AGL; don't attempt turns at low altitude; due to inertia the main wheels may briefly touch the runway - do not pull back excessively to prevent this and do not deliberately land; then proceed as a go-around.

questions.prompt: Recite the crash drill items exactly as used in the SEFATO / forced landing context, including which items are touch-drill only.
questions.model_answer: Crash drill: Seat belts - fastened; Fuel selector - closed (T); Flaps - set; Electric Master - off (T). (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY.
questions.explanation: The QRC crash drills list: seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T), where (T) means touch drill only. The crash drill is step 8 of the SEFATO procedure in the circuit emergencies exercise.
